title: Bid, ask and the spread
desc: The toll you pay on every trade

cards.title: Where did the $0.10 go?
cards.situation: You buy a stock at $50.05. A second later your position shows −$0.10 a share, but the price didn’t move. Where did it go?

options.feedback: Not a bug. Your app shows what you’d get selling now, and that’s less than you paid.
Nobody took it. Your app values your share at what you’d get selling now, a bit less than you paid.

options.text: You paid a toll for buying instantly
options.feedback: Buying now costs a bit more than selling now. That gap is the toll for trading instantly.

cards.added: Feedback for B written for the Academy

cards.title: Two prices, not one
cards.text: The price on your screen is the **last handshake**: the latest deal.

blocks.p: Right now there are two prices: the **[[bid|bid]]** (from buyers) and the **[[ask|ask]]** (from sellers). The gap is the **[[spread|spread]]**. Your app values your shares at the bid.

blocks.tip: You {up}buy at the ask{/up} and {down}sell at the bid{/down}: every [[round-trip|round trip]] pays the spread.

cards.title: Round trip, no move
cards.q: You buy {n} shares and sell them straight away. The price doesn’t move. What’s your result?

options.feedback: The price didn’t move, but you bought at the higher ask and sold at the lower bid.
You can’t gain when the price stands still. You bought at the higher ask and sold at the lower bid.
You bought at the ask and sold at the bid, so you paid the spread on every share.
That’s only half the gap. On a round trip you pay the full spread on every share.

cards.added: Feedback for B, C and D from the earlier lesson, shortened

cards.title: The fee that eats over-traders
cards.text: Every round trip pays the spread, even when the price never moves. Trade a lot, and it adds up fast.
cards.rule: fewer, better trades beat many average ones.

cards.title: Tight toll, wide toll
cards.text: **[[liquidity|Liquidity]]** is how easily you can buy or sell without moving the price. The more people trade something, the smaller the spread.

head.title: Busy stock
head.sub: Millions of shares trade every day

blocks.tip: Low liquidity also means you might be the only one trying to sell.

cards.title: The day trader’s bill
cards.q: A day trader makes 500 round trips a year. The spread costs him $10 each time. What does he pay in a year?

options.feedback: $10 is the cost of one round trip. He makes 500 of them, and pays the toll every time.
He pays the toll on every single round trip, and each one costs $10.
He pays $10 on every one of his 500 round trips. An investor with one round trip pays $10.
That’s ten times too much. Multiply the 500 round trips by the $10 each one costs.

cards.work: 500 round trips × $10 = $5,000 a year. An investor with 1 round trip pays $10.
cards.added: Feedback for A, C and D written for the Academy

cards.headline: You can spot the toll on any trade.
lines: You buy at the ask and sell at the bid. The gap is the spread.
The spread is a toll on every round trip, even if the price never moves.
Busy markets and fewer trades keep the toll small.
